original_question: Find a bound for |μ(σ, τ)| in the permutation pattern poset that depends only on the number of occurrences of σ in τ, without requiring additional structure such as separability.
target_in_paper: Section 5.1 of arXiv:1210.7320, in the paragraph near the end of the Möbius-function discussion that says: "Another question raised in [19] is whether it is possible to find a bound on |μ(σ,τ)| that depends only on the number of occurrences of σ in τ." The exact formal source that this sentence points to is Section 5, Question 29 of Burstein–Jelínek–Jelínková–Steingrímsson, which asks for an upper bound for |μ(σ,π)| depending only on σ(π).
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right invariant (the Möbius function μ of an interval in the permutation pattern poset), the right quantity it should depend on (the number of occurrences of σ in τ), and the key intent of removing special hypotheses such as separability. It is therefore aimed at the general open-question direction highlighted in Section 5.1, not at the narrower separable or 132-avoiding results.
missing_details: It should explicitly quantify over all finite permutations σ and τ with σ ≤ τ in the classical permutation pattern poset.
It should define the ambient poset: permutations ordered by classical pattern containment.
It should define σ(τ) as the number of occurrences of σ as a pattern in τ.
It should phrase the problem as an existence question for a universal function F depending only on one integer argument, namely σ(τ).
It should specify that the same bound F must work uniformly for every interval [σ,τ], not vary with σ or τ separately.
It should make clear that this is an upper-bound question, not necessarily the specific bound |μ(σ,τ)| ≤ σ(τ), which is only known in special classes such as separable permutations.
It should note that no extra structural assumptions (such as separability or 132-avoidance) are to be imposed, since those belong only to background results motivating the open problem.
refined_question: Let P be the poset of all finite permutations ordered by classical pattern containment. For permutations σ and τ with σ ≤ τ, let μ(σ,τ) denote the Möbius function of the interval [σ,τ], and let σ(τ) denote the number of occurrences of σ as a pattern in τ. Does there exist a universal function F: N -> N such that |μ(σ,τ)| <= F(σ(τ)) for every interval [σ,τ] in P, without imposing additional hypotheses on σ or τ such as separability or pattern-avoidance restrictions?
justification: The draft is not best matched to the narrower 132-avoiding conjecture or the separable-permutation corollary. Instead, it matches the broader open problem explicitly singled out in Section 5.1 of the survey and formalized as Question 29 in the cited paper on separable and decomposable permutations. The survey first recalls that for separable permutations one has the occurrence-count bound, and then asks whether any bound depending only on the occurrence count exists in general. That is exactly the intent your draft is trying to capture.
